title: Megalomaniac: Random Notable Allocation, Trade Search and Value Filters (0.5.4)
summary: Megalomaniac is a Unique Diamond Jewel in Path of Exile 2 0.5.4 that allocates 2-3 random Notable Passive Skills from your passive tree, saving the points you would spend reaching them. This guide covers the notable value model, the notable classification table, how to search two or three specific notables on the trade site, the Simulacrum drop, valuation, and community questions.
description: How Megalomaniac works in PoE2 0.5.4: the Diamond Jewel that grants 2-3 random Notables, the notable value model, trade search UI steps, Simulacrum drop, valuation, and community questions.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: Path of Exile 2 Megalomaniac unique Diamond Jewel allocating random Notable Passive Skills on the passive skill tree

sections.title: Quick answer
sections.callout: Megalomaniac is a Unique Diamond Jewel that allocates 2-3 random Notable Passive Skills from your passive tree the moment it is socketed - as if you had travelled to each notable and spent the points yourself, except the points stay in your pool. It is Limited to 1, always Corrupted on drop (so it cannot be rerolled), and in 0.5.4 it drops only from the Simulacrum's Delirium bosses. Its value is entirely the roll: three notables useful for a meta build can be worth hundreds of Divine Orbs, while an off-build roll is near-worthless.
calloutDetail: The notables are fully random and cannot repeat; you cannot pick them at drop.
Because it is Corrupted on drop, no Vaal, Chaos, or Divine Orb can change which notables it grants.

answers.label: Use for
text: Reclaiming the passive points you would otherwise spend pathing to deep, build-defining Notables.

answers.label: Check first
text: Read the exact notable names (web trade site shows full descriptions) and confirm they fit your build before buying; do not trust the jewel title.

answers.label: Avoid
text: Assuming a three-notable jewel is automatically valuable, or trying to equip two Megalomaniacs - only one is allowed.

sections.title: Family overview: Diamond Unique Jewels
intro: Megalomaniac is part of the Diamond Unique Jewel family - jewels that rewrite how a passive-tree socket behaves. Each member solves a different tree problem; Megalomaniac is the random-Notable member.

sections.note: A three-notable jewel where two notables are strong for your build and one is filler is still an excellent buy - you reclaim two notables' worth of points plus a real stat spread.

sections.title: Overview and current versus legacy
paragraphs: Megalomaniac collapses the cost of reaching good Notables into a single socket. Socket it into an allocated jewel socket and it immediately grants the effects of whatever 2-3 Notables it rolled, exactly as if you had walked to each and spent the points - except the points stay in your pool to spend elsewhere. Notables are the large, named passives with icons and multi-line text; the jewel effectively anoints two or three of them at once, for free.

Because the notables are random and the jewel is Corrupted on drop, Megalomaniac is a lottery, not a crafting target. Most drops are junk for any given build, but a jewel that is junk for you can be perfect for someone else, which is why its trade market is huge. Value follows the notable value model: net value equals the effective notables gained, plus the value of pathing saved, minus one jewel socket, minus the pathing to the socket, minus the Rare/Unique jewel you gave up.

Current versus legacy: since patch 0.5.0 Megalomaniac drops identified, so you see the rolled Notables immediately instead of needing to identify it. The allocation behaviour (2-3 random Notables, no duplicates) is unchanged from earlier in Early Access. The Simulacrum remains the only source.
bullets: Current (0.5.4): drops identified; allocates 2-3 random Notables; Simulacrum-only drop.
Patch 0.5.0 change: Megalomaniac now drops identified (previously unidentified).
The jewel is always Corrupted; the notables can never be rerolled or changed.
Only one Megalomaniac may be socketed per character.

sections.title: Eligibility: what is required
note: Megalomaniac has almost no preconditions - it grants its notables the instant it is socketed, with no pathing or connection requirement.

values.text: Must be socketed in an allocated passive-tree jewel socket.
Notables are granted without pathing to them.
Points normally spent are refunded to spend elsewhere.
The roll cannot duplicate a Notable.
Always Corrupted on drop; not modifyable.

steps.label: Identify the Notables your build wants
body: Decide which 2-3 Notables would save you the most pathing on your current tree. Deep, build-defining Notables are worth the most.

steps.label: Socket Megalomaniac in an allocated slot
body: Place it in any allocated jewel socket. The rolled Notables are granted instantly and the saved points return to your pool.

steps.label: Spend the reclaimed points
body: Use the freed points to deepen another cluster or fix a defensive gap - that is the real payoff.

steps.label: Search the trade site for specific Notables
body: On the official trade site: set Item Category to Jewel, Rarity to Unique, and type the exact name 'Megalomaniac'. Add a Stat Filter for 'Allocates Passive Skill' and repeat it for a second (and third) Notable you want. Set League to the current league and toggle Online/Offline as needed.

steps.label: Read full notable descriptions before buying
body: The in-game client shows only notable names; open the trade listing in a web browser to see full descriptions on hover, or check PoE2DB / PoE2Wiki for the exact notable. Never buy on the jewel title alone.

before: Reaching three deep Notables might cost 15-60 passive points of pathing you do not have.
after: Megalomaniac grants those same Notables from one socket and returns the points to your pool.
compare.note: Value is the pathing saved, not the jewel itself - a notable one node off your path is barely worth anything.

rows.scenario: Three Notables match your meta build
rows.recommendation: Buy the exact roll; it is one of the best point-efficiency upgrades available.
Do not buy a roll that does not fit; sell it to the build that wants it.

rows.benefit: Two Notables' worth of points plus a stat spread
rows.recommendation: Still an excellent buy; you rarely need all three to be perfect.

rows.benefit: Volume play; sell to other builds
rows.recommendation: Push Simulacrum difficulty high and farm volume; most drops are inventory to sell.

sections.title: Build usage
intro: Megalomaniac is build-agnostic but roll-specific. The decision below shows when to commit to buying one.

builds.title: Deep-cluster Path of Exile 2 builds
builds.description: Any build that would otherwise path deep into a far cluster to grab a key Notable benefits most from a matching Megalomaniac.

builds.title: Mana-stacker Archmage
builds.description: A Megalomaniac with Mental Perseverance is effectively mandatory for some Archmage setups, paired with a Heart of the Well jewel.

builds.title: Crit and damage-multiplier builds
builds.description: Notables granting crit multi or a damage-type multiplier your build already scales are worth far more than flat attribute notables.

builds.title: Point-starved league starters
builds.description: A well-sniped Megalomaniac converts modest currency into 20-60 reclaimed points once the build is online.

sections.title: Alternatives
paragraphs: If you cannot find a matching roll, a Rare Diamond Jewel or another Diamond Unique may serve better. From Nothing grants a random Keystone (useful when a single Keystone is the goal), while Against the Darkness reshapes the small passives around its socket for attribute or defence stacking.
Anointment on an amulet grants one Notable at a time and is fully chooseable, so for a single critical Notable an anointment is more reliable than gambling on Megalomaniac's random roll.
Timeless Jewels and Cluster-style setups are complementary ways to reshape the tree, but none replicate Megalomaniac's free 2-3 Notable allocation.
bullets: Amulet anointment: one chooseable Notable, no RNG.
From Nothing: one random Keystone instead of Notables.
Against the Darkness: radius small-passive modifiers, not Notables.

marketNote: Prices below reflect the Early Access 0.5.4 league on the PC trade site as of early August 2026 and move constantly with supply and demand.
Value is almost entirely the roll: a jewel with three Notables useful for a meta build can be worth hundreds of Divine Orbs, while an off-build roll is worth less than a Regal Orb.

entries.question: Why can't I find a specific Notable when searching Megalomaniac?
summary: A player asked why filtering for an exact Notable returned few or no results.
editorialAnalysis: Notables are random per jewel and the in-game client shows only names. Use the web trade site with repeated 'Allocates Passive Skill' stat filters, and read full descriptions on hover before buying.
officialAnswer: Each Megalomaniac rolls random Notables; search by exact notable name with multiple stat filters on the web trade site.

entries.question: Can I equip two Megalomaniacs or reroll the Notables?
summary: A guide explained the equip limit and corruption lock.
editorialAnalysis: Megalomaniac is Limited to 1 and always Corrupted on drop, so no Vaal, Chaos, or Divine Orb can change its Notables. The only way to 'reroll' is a different jewel.
officialAnswer: One Megalomaniac per tree; the rolled Notables are permanent.

entries.question: Why does a three-Notable jewel sometimes have no value?
summary: A guide explained the roll-dependent value swing.
editorialAnalysis: A three-Notable jewel where none of the Notables fit a build is worth less than a Regal Orb, while the same item with meta-build Notables sells for hundreds of Divines. Value is always relative to a specific build.
officialAnswer: Value follows the roll; off-build Notables are near-worthless, meta-build Notables are premium.

entries.question: How do I read what a Megalomaniac's Notables actually do before buying?
summary: A video walked through vetting a Megalomaniac on the trade site.
editorialAnalysis: Open the trade listing in a browser to see full notable descriptions on hover, or check PoE2DB / PoE2Wiki for the exact notable and its tree position to judge points saved.
officialAnswer: Use the web trade site hover or a database entry to read each Notable before spending.

problems.symptom: Search returns no Megalomaniac with my Notable
directAnswer: Notables are random per jewel. Use the web trade site with repeated 'Allocates Passive Skill' stat filters for each Notable you want, and widen Online/Offline and price if needed.
checks: Add one 'Allocates Passive Skill' stat filter per target Notable.
Confirm the exact notable spelling on PoE2DB before filtering.

problems.symptom: The jewel shows names but not what they do
directAnswer: The in-game client shows only Notable names. Open the trade listing in a web browser to see full descriptions, or check a database entry.
checks: Hover the listing on the web trade site, or search the notable name on PoE2DB / PoE2Wiki.

problems.symptom: Vaal/Divine Orb did nothing to the Notables
directAnswer: Megalomaniac is Corrupted on drop; the Notables are permanent and cannot be changed by any currency.
checks: Only a different Megalomaniac changes the rolled Notables.

directAnswer: The jewel is Limited to 1; only one Megalomaniac may be socketed per character.
checks: Keep the second copy to sell or trade, not to equip.
